paragraphs.text: Warhammer 40,000 or Warhammer 40K (stylized as Warhammer 40,000 Commander Decks ) is a product in the Magic: The Gathering Universes Beyond series released by Wizards of the Coast . Warhammer 40K was released on October 7, 2022. The release of the set was originally slated for August 12, 2022, but it was delayed due to ongoing supply chain complications.

This is a cross-over product based on the Warhammer 40,000 miniature wargame produced by Games Workshop . The set introduces 42 new Warhammer 40K -themed cards in each deck, featuring the triangular holofoil stamp of non-canon cards. Reprints (#169-317) also feature art set in the world of Warhammer 40K . Card numbers #318-321 are the display commanders . Card number #322 is an unreleased promo.
Warhammer’s world isn’t evenly color-balanced as it wasn't created with the color pie in mind. R&D solved this problem by making Commander decks instead of a full set.
There are no current plans to make in-universe Magic versions of the new cards in the Warhammer 40K Commander decks , but R&D can do it if needed on a card-by-card basis.

There are 168 different mechanically new cards printed in the Warhammer 40,000 Commander Decks. These cards are legal for play in the Commander , Vintage , and Legacy formats. They aren't legal for play in the Standard , Pioneer , or Modern formats. Foil versions of the commanders and surge foil display versions of the face commanders are numbered 169-180. The release card is #181.
Each package contains:
A 99-card deck, including 1 foil backup commander
1 foil face Commander 1 foil-etched display version of the face commander
10 double-sided tokens

Most Warhammer 40K fiction is set around the turn of the 41st millennium (about 38,000 years in the future). Although Warhammer 40K is mostly a science-fiction setting, it adapts several tropes from fantasy fiction, such as magic , daemons , and races such as Orks ( Orcs ) and Eldar ( Elves ); "psykers" fill the role of wizards in the setting.

Warhammer 40,000 consists of four Commander decks, showing off the Imperium of Man , the Forces of Chaos , the undying Necrons and the Tyranids . The four 100-card decks contain 168 new cards in total. Each deck plays true to the army's heroes, strategies and lore, and comes with a Sol Ring themed around its faction.

The four commander decks are also available in a Collector's Edition with a unique "Universes Beyond" card frame . The Collector's Edition comes fully foiled with the never-before-seen special surge foil and has the same card content. A complete set costs about 550 dollars.
The set is accompanied by three Secret Lairs featuring the same IP. All three were released in the October Superdrop 2022 .
Secret Lair Drop Series: Warhammer 40,000: Orks
Secret Lair Drop Series: Warhammer Age of Sigmar
Secret Lair Drop Series: Blood Bowl
Launch Weekend : October 7–9, 2022
Release card : Fabricate
Gatherer features an unreleased Adaptive Automaton promo card.

At the time of release, a development pathway to bring the decks to Magic Online hadn't been established. The original plan was to program only the cards that impacted the paper metagame for Commander or other eternal formats and release them as part of the Treasure Chest reward system but this was soon abandoned due to the IP contracts surrounding the Universes Beyond licensing. The digital licensing contract only allowed for the cards to be sold as complete 100-card decks, resulting in the Magic Online development team having to program the cards between premier set releases. A tentative digital release had been outlined for Q3 2023, depending on finalization of the IP contract with Games Workshop, but was ultimately missed. The decks finally became available in Magic Online on February 21, 2024 for $39.99 each. The sale period for the decks was only sixty days, with the last day to purchase on April 5, 2024.

On August 18, 2026 the Magic Online team announced that all four of the decks would go on sale for a second time from 10 a.m. on August 19. As with their original sale, the decks were priced at $39.99 each and cards from the decks would not be made available in Treasure Chests. The sale period runs from August 19 until "the end of 2026".

Multiplayer Commander is not an available format on Magic: The Gathering Arena and commander-only products, where the new card designs are only legal in eternal formats, are not added to the platform.
Warhammer 40,000 Commander Decks is multicolor themed, and many cards use flavor words .
Each preconstructed deck was designed with a theme for each tribe:
Tyranid Swarm ( , +1/+1 counters and aggro)
The Ruinous Powers ( , Instant and sorceries, and Lifeloss)
Necron Dynasties ( , Artifacts and graveyard interactions)
Forces of the Imperium( , Tokens and go wide)

Forces of the Imperium introduces the Squad mechanic that allows paying an extra casting cost any number of times to make that many copies of the spell. It also uses the Miracle mechanic from Avacyn Restored on several cards. It provides an alternative cost for a card if it is the first card drawn during a turn. In this set, it is used on permanents for the first time.
Tyranid Swarm introduces the Ravenous mechanic that allows players to draw a card from their cost creatures if they spend five or more mana on X.
Necron Dynasties uses the Unearth mechanic that allows you to return cards from your graveyard, but exiling them at the end step.
The Ruinous Powers features the Cascade mechanic that allows you to cast nonland cards with lower mana value, from your library, without paying their mana cost.
The set introduces the Astartes , C'Tan , Custodes , Necron , Primarch , Robot , and Tyranid creature types . It reintroduces the Inquisitor type.
The set introduces Necrodermis counters and saw the return of Eon counters and Infection counters .
Warhammer 40,000 Commander Decks has three cycles .

Warhammer 40K was favorably received, thanks to the gameplay and the value of the decks. The set had at least four reprints. Hasbro CEO Chris Cocks called it “one of our best-selling Commander decks ever”.
